relevance_note: Case report of a woman with a LAMP2 variant and Danon disease, plus a hemizygous carrier son and wild-type tested relatives: "identified a heterozygous frameshift variant in LAMP2".
method_note: Read the paper in full by hand; the JSON was assembled with a short Python script whose values were typed from that reading (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). Labels: the proband has no own label ('the proband', 'the patient' are role words), so 'patient' (rule 5); relatives are '<relation as written> of patient'. Mother, father and younger brother are in scope as tested-negative relatives (wild-type on Sanger) and get no variant rows. Variants in BBS1, DCHS1, VWF, RYR2 and CYP4V2 are named but not described (no printed variant) and called VUS without phenotypic correlation, so they get no rows. Proband inheritance recorded as 'de novo' because both parents were tested wild-type (rule 8), but the authors themselves say this 'suggests a de novo event or parental germline mosaicism'. Son's inheritance recorded as 'inherited maternal' because his mother (the proband) is stated to carry the same deletion. Son's variant string, type, pathogenicity and ACMG codes come from sentences naming this exact variant plus 'Detection of the same variant in the patient's son'. Pathogenicity: the commercial laboratory first called the variant of uncertain significance; the authors reclassified it as likely pathogenic (recorded). Age at onset taken as the age at the initial stroke-like presentation (27 years); exertional dyspnea for two months before the March 2019 admission is not dated relative to the stroke. Age at diagnosis and at last follow-up (18 months later) are not stated. n_patients_reported left null: the authors do not state a count (one proband with Danon disease and one carrier son are described). Left ventricular hypertrophy left 'not reported': septum 10.3 mm and posterior wall 11.6 mm are given without interpretation, and the Discussion's 'relatively preserved septal thickness' is hedged. 'Proximal muscle weakness (skeletal myopathy)' left 'not reported': normal strength on examination and no prior neuromuscular symptoms do not address the broader composite item (CK was above the reference range). 'Elevated liver enzymes' left 'not reported': 'Liver function ... unremarkable' is a whole-panel normal result (D-27), recorded only as excluded 'abnormal liver function'; likewise renal function, coagulation, autoantibodies and serologies are recorded as the paper names them. Elevated creatine kinase recorded as observed from the value above the printed reference range (299.1 U/L, reference 105-245); the paper does not use the word 'elevated' for CK. 'Cardioembolic stroke' not recorded as a feature because the paper says consensus 'favored' it (hedged). Apparent contradictions / time differences: the abstract says 'physical and neurological examinations were unremarkable' whereas the text reports a soft holosystolic murmur at the apex on examination (murmur recorded as observed; no whole-exam row emitted). Initial MRA showed distal right middle cerebral artery narrowing, while later duplex examinations documented normal carotid and intracranial arteries ('normal vascular imaging on follow-up'); both rows are emitted (neither is a checklist item). Muscle weakness 'excluded' refers to the normal strength at admission for etiologic evaluation, after the earlier left-sided weakness (observed) had resolved. Son's age is not stated (the proband delivered him at age 21); his phenotype is not described, so all his checklist items are 'not reported'. Maternal hypertension recorded as an observed feature of the mother.
